definition: Hierarchical Navigable Small World, a graph-based algorithm for efficient approximate nearest-neighbor search in high-dimensional vector spaces.
details: HNSW is one of the most widely used indexing algorithms in vector databases, offering a strong balance of search speed, accuracy, and memory usage.
story: Think of a historian sorting through boxes of letters, building a picture of an era one sentence at a time. Every machine is shaped by what it was shown, so someone has to choose that material with care. The examples a machine reads become the world it believes in. The words a model reads become the world it believes in. And that is HNSW — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.

citation.title: Efficient and Robust Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search Using Hierarchical Navigable Small World Graphs
citation.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
